# Read and derived staleness: is this moment mine?

## What this region is

Reading a gloss with staleness derived from git at read time: when each note was written against how often its symbol's code changed since, plus the per-section history and the git helpers that compute both.

## What it exists for

- Show or judge how current a margin note is
- Look at a gloss from the shell
- Keep files out of enumeration (both internal)

## How people say these problems

A moment that says any of these, or something close, is this region's. Both voices: the user asking or correcting, and the agent describing what it is about to build.

- is this note out of date
- how many times did the code change since the note
- show the note with its freshness
- list the commits that touched this section
- print the note for this file
- show how this section changed over time
- read the margin for one symbol
- skip ignored files when scanning
- leave the vendored tree alone
- why was this file not linted
- add a last updated date to each note
- is the whole note file older than the code
- show the history of one section from the shell
- print the margin note for this file
- while changing gloss, handle repos without git when filtering
- while changing gloss, match excludes at folder boundaries
- show the note with its freshness header
- list the commits that changed this section
- has this function changed since its note was written
- track when notes were written in the file
- get a staleness verdict for one file's gloss
- see older versions of this note
- read the note for one symbol from the terminal
- treat nothing ignored as filter nothing
- make the exclude check prefix only, no regex
- I'll read the sidecar file and print it raw
- show how this note evolved in git

- how stale is this one symbol's note

## When this is not your domain

These mention this region's words but belong elsewhere; the answer is no, and the region named answers instead.

- parse the margin file into its sections so I can edit one → sidecar-harvest-and-check
- skip the vendored folder when scanning files → comment-rule-and-source-scanning
- the check reports a section whose marker was deleted → sidecar-harvest-and-check
- append the margin note whenever the agent reads a file → agent-integration-setup-and-cli
